title: Luminescent radicals – synthesis, photophysics and applications
content: Although known for over a century, radicals have only now begun playing a role in the chemistry of π-conjugated materials. Over the past two decades, following Juliá's discovery that a Ballester-type radical bearing a single carbazole substituent can achieve a photoluminescence quantum yield of 53%, luminescent radicals have progressed from a scientific curiosity to a well-established research field. Although the chemical space of luminescent radicals is rather limited and the details of their photophysics still require better understanding, the field continues to fascinate and challenge researchers. In this review, we present all aspects of the chemistry of luminescent radicals, starting with general photophysical considerations, moving through synthetic developments and structure–property relationship, before discussing computational aspects and various applications. A detailed analysis of the advances made since 2006 highlights the contributions of multiple research groups that have continually expanded the structural landscape of luminescent radicals. Particular emphasis is placed on synthetic aspects, as the availability of robust synthetic methodologies is often a bottleneck, limiting progress in materials-oriented research.
